_doc: The shared drives WP-H1 ingests, and the visibility everything derived from
each one inherits (ADR-0013).
Starting set, chosen 2026-08-28: the three drives every employee can already
read. That is deliberate as a first cut — a drive whose membership is the
whole company cannot leak to the whole company, so the isolation tests can
come before the drives that need them rather than after.
NO ADDRESSABLE IDENTIFIER LIVES IN THIS FILE, deliberately. The drive and
space ids are in the event_sources table, seeded by migration
0045_seed_event_sources.sql, and that is what the connector and the
reconciler read. They were enumerated 2026-08-30 via drives.list under
domain-wide delegation, because matching by NAME would have been ambiguous:
the tenant has ten shared drives and three of them begin with "BizDev" —
BizDev, BizDev DataHub and "BizDev <-> Ops". An id is what the API takes and
the only thing a rename does not move. The names below are labels for
whoever reads this file, not how anything is matched.
This file carries the subscription SHAPE and the visibility policy. It is
compiled into the binary (go:embed) and the repository is public, which is
no place for live meeting and drive identifiers — they grant nothing
without Workspace membership, but they are operational and they need not be
here to do their job.
Adding a drive with narrower membership means adding it with the visibility
its membership implies — NOT internal. ADR-0013 makes every derived artefact
inherit the strictest classification of its sources, so getting this wrong
here is how a client-confidential document ends up quoted in a summary that
the whole company can read.

drives.name: All
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company

drives.name: BizDev
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company

drives.name: Delivery
drives.why: readable by everyone in the company

_doc: The Drive subscription shape that validates against these drives, established
by probing each field and each event type on 2026-08-30 rather than from the
documentation — which lists types that a shared-drive target rejects.
includeDescendants must be true and is IMMUTABLE. A shared-drive subscription
without it is refused outright, and one created with it cannot be changed, so
this is not a default to discover later.
Two documented types are NOT in the list, and for different reasons:
file.v3.content    'One or more event types are incorrectly formatted' —
not valid against a shared-drive target at all.
file.v3.untrashed  PERMISSION_DENIED, consistently, on a scope that accepts
trashed. So a file restored from the bin raises no event
and ingestion will not see it come back. Reconciliation
has to cover that, or the gap has to be accepted
deliberately — widening the scope to close it is a
domain-wide grant and a worse trade.
drive_subscription.verified: 2026-08-30, validateOnly against All, BizDev and Delivery

_doc: The registered recurring Meet (wg-8yv.38, chosen 2026-08-30).
Innovation Team Sync, Monday to Thursday, used for the DataHub.io product.
Transcription is on by default for it, which is what makes it ingestable at
all — events fire whether or not a transcript exists, and a meeting with
transcription off produces events carrying nothing.
The meeting is SOMETIMES SKIPPED. A week with no transcript is therefore
silence, not an incident, and monitoring separates the two: subscription
health is alerted on, content arrival is not. What IS an incident is a
conference record existing with no transcript retrieved, because that is
the shape of ingestion breaking rather than of a quiet week (ADR-0027).
internal because the attendees are Datopian staff and the subject is our own
product. A client-confidential meeting would need its own visibility and
would not belong in the same registry entry (ADR-0013).
The space itself is identified in event_sources (migration 0045), not here.
A typeable meeting code is only an alias for it, and an alias is the same
trap as a drive name: human, rotatable, and not what the API is stable on.
Verified by probing on 2026-08-30. transcript.v2.file and recording.v2.file
are documented and REJECTED as 'incorrectly formatted', the same way
file.v3.content is for drives.
Two types, and the pair is the design. conference.v2.ended says a meeting
happened; transcript.v2.ended says a transcript is retrievable. Together they
separate the two silences ADR-0027 cares about: no conference event at all is
a skipped meeting and not an incident, while a conference that ended with no
transcript following is ingestion breaking.
participant.v2.joined validates and is deliberately NOT subscribed to. It is
attendance data we have no use for, and least privilege applies to what we
collect as much as to what we can reach.
